trajectory_summary: The call opens cold and drifts through a mechanical verify sequence with no real rapport built, then breaks down entirely when the credit/tax qualifier triggers a privacy objection the rep cannot resolve. The rep repeats the same scripted reassurance three times without adapting, and the customer terminates the call having given no bill, no real interest reason, and no appointment.

observed_outcome.reasoning: The customer explicitly refuses to continue and ends the call before any appointment, bill collection, or button-up occurred; there is no next step owned by the rep.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call never reached bill collection — it broke down at the credit/tax qualifier stage when the customer refused to continue, so no bill amount or usage figure was ever discussed.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked the interest question and got a vague answer, restated it back once ('So you're pretty much just curious about it?') but never developed it into a hook used later in the pitch or at any recovery point during the objection.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: I just don't like giving out personal information to a person that calls me on the phone.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer raised the same privacy/legitimacy concern three times (02:41, 03:16, 03:38) and the rep answered with the same generic line each time instead of escalating with specifics — this is the exact opposite of multi_angle_resilience and is the direct cause of the call's collapse.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Well, I'll be quick with you.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep skips any real legitimacy framing (no mention of how the lead was generated, no state reference, no form/Tesla anchor) and instead leads with a promise of brevity, which undercuts trust-building before qualification even starts.

key_moments.quote: I don't know. I would I you know, I would just wanted to look into it.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer's interest reason is thin and unresolved ('just wanted to look into it'), and the rep accepts it at face value without probing for a real motivator (bill pain, environmental concern, etc.) that could later anchor the pitch.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Gotcha. So you're pretty much just curious about it?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep restates the customer's vague answer back to her rather than expanding it, confirming the interest reason was logged but never developed into something usable later in the call.

key_moments.quote: just to qualify for the new furnace.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep substitutes 'furnace' for 'solar' mid-qualifier — likely a copy-paste script artifact from another vertical/campaign rather than a deliberate choice, and it happens right before the sensitive credit/income ask.
